page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server is equipped with 3780 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10%. The Neoverse-N2 architecture delivers strong memory bandwidth, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 465.57 GB/sec and write speeds at 203.79 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations also rank in the top 10%, reflecting high parallel processing efficiency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64plds_v6 offers a high density of physical ARM cores and substantial local storage, making it highly resource-efficient for parallelized compute tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This server is optimized for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data decompression.
